I'm not familiar with loop quantum gravity, but what this article is describing is already true with our current understanding. Nothing in our perceived universe can ever actually enter into a black hole. As one approaches the event horizon of a black hole the gravitational time dilation effect approaches infinity. What this means is that from our perspective something would be constantly approaches a black hole but never quite get there. The visible light would quickly end up getting red shifted into invisibility, but the object nonetheless never enters into the blackhole - it stays 'stuck' to the outside for all of eternity from an observer's point of view. This actually leads to a fun question about how then black holes - let alone super massives - could form in the first place, but that's another topic altogether!
